subject: Career
title: Illegal Questions and How to Deflect
description: A quick win: understand Illegal Questions and How to Deflect.

hook.text: 'Are you planning to have kids?' It's illegal in many places. But it still gets asked.

buildup.text: Questions about age, religion, marital status, and pregnancy are off-limits in most jurisdictions.

discovery.text: The interviewer may not know it's illegal. Assume ignorance before malice.

twist.text: A graceful redirect works: 'I'm fully committed to this role. Can I tell you about my availability?'

climax.text: If the question feels targeted or hostile, it's a data point about the company's culture.

punchline.text: How they interview tells you how they manage.

quiz.question: What's the best way to handle an illegal interview question?

details.summary: Some interview questions about age, marital status, religion, or family planning are illegal in many jurisdictions. Knowing your rights and having prepared deflection strategies protects you while maintaining a positive rapport.
details.whyItMatters: Candidates who are caught off guard by illegal questions either overshare or react defensively, both of which harm their candidacy. Preparation turns an awkward moment into a smooth redirect.
takeaways: Familiarize yourself with protected categories in your jurisdiction
Redirect to the underlying job-related concern behind the question
Document the question if you choose to report it later

faq.question: What are the most common illegal interview questions candidates encounter?
faq.answer: Questions about age, marital status, number of children, religious practices, national origin, and disability status are among the most common. Sometimes they are asked indirectly, like 'what year did you graduate' as a proxy for age.

faq.question: How do you deflect an illegal question without creating an adversarial atmosphere?
faq.answer: Address the legitimate concern behind the question. If asked about children, respond with 'I am fully committed to the demands of this role and have a strong track record of meeting deadlines.' This reassures without disclosing protected information.
